title: IRC: a keyed call starting elsewhere should be a notice, not a silence or a trap
description:
Raised 2026-11-23 when Mark asked what an IRC user does about a call.

THE SITUATION. IRC already carries the LINK kind of call
(bead mimid-1wgh.114.3: the `call` command, Store::send_call, the ACTION
line). It cannot carry the KEYED kind: a stock IRC client has no media
stack, so there is nothing to hand a media secret to, and no way to
exchange SDP.

TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT:

1. A KEYED CALL STARTED ELSEWHERE must be visible. The announcement of
   bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 arrives as a message in the parent chat, so IRC
   will render whatever text it carries -- that is the point of putting
   the human-readable sentence in a message rather than only in an
   extension key. What IRC should NOT do is show it as a joinable
   thing. A notice naming who started it, and saying this client cannot
   join, is the honest rendering.

2. IRC MUST NOT OFFER TO START ONE. A `/call` that hosted a
   parent-dependent room from IRC would make a room nobody on IRC could
   join with media: the user would see a call that silently does
   nothing. If the command is offered at all it should refuse with a
   sentence saying why, which is more use than a call that fails
   quietly.

DO NOT confuse this with giving IRC the keyed call. It cannot have it.
This bead is about the two ways IRC can be wrong about a call it cannot
join.
notes:
BOTH ITEMS DONE, 2026-11-24, now that bead mimid-1wgh.114.1's
announcement exists.

ITEM 1, the notice. A message carrying the call announcement renders as a
server NOTICE naming who started it and saying this client cannot join,
INSTEAD OF the plain PRIVMSG rather than beside it
(mimid-agent-irc/src/render.rs message_lines, which returns early, and
call_notice). "alice started a video call: standup -- this client cannot
join it". An ended announcement drops the "cannot join" half, since there
is nothing left to join and repeating it would be noise.

Replacing rather than adding is the point. The bead's two failure modes
are a SILENCE and a TRAP; rendering the sentence as an ordinary message
is the trap, because a stock IRC client has no media stack and no way to
exchange SDP, so the line would offer something that silently does
nothing. One notice is the honest third thing.

ITEM 2 needed no new refusal, and the earlier note on this bead was right
that IRC cannot start a keyed call: the `call` command requires a URL, so
it structurally cannot host a parent-dependent room. What it DID need was
a sentence: `call #chat` with no URL used to answer "usage: call #channel
<url> [<description>]", which tells a user who meant "start a call"
nothing about why they cannot. It now says a URL is required because IRC
can send a link to a call hosted elsewhere but cannot host one itself
(service.rs CALL_USAGE). The link kind of call (bead mimid-1wgh.114.3)
still works and is unchanged.

TESTS, both in crates/mimid-agent/tests/irc_v2.rs against a real daemon
and IRC connection:

  - a_keyed_call_is_a_notice_that_irc_cannot_join_it: a call started in a
    chat gives a NOTICE in that chat's channel, saying "cannot join",
    naming the kind ("video call") and the subject. It asserts the notice
    carries the MESSAGE'S OWN msgid, which is what proves the notice
    REPLACED the rendering instead of arriving beside a PRIVMSG: a
    message's tags go on the first line of its rendering. It also
    asserts the call room has no IRC channel, so there is nothing to
    join by mistake.
  - call_without_a_url_says_irc_cannot_host_one.

A NOTE ON MY OWN TEST, since it is the kind of thing worth recording: the
first version asserted `!notice.raw.contains("PRIVMSG")`, which on a
NOTICE line cannot fail and therefore tested nothing. Replaced with the
msgid check above, which can.

DOCUMENTED: crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/lib.rs's front-end summary, and
docs/agent.md's [irc] section ("Calls on IRC").

STILL OPEN, and recorded on this bead rather than silently dropped: an
INVITE to a call room cannot be told apart from any other invite, because
record::Invite has no parent field -- Agent::invite_details does not
surface the Welcome's parent_room. With `invites = "any"` it never shows;
with a stricter policy an IRC user gets a pending invite to something
they cannot use, and the notice does not help because the invite arrives
on its own path. Fixing it is work in mimid-agent-core, not here.
close_reason: Both items done. Item 1: a call announcement renders as a server NOTICE saying this client cannot join, instead of the PRIVMSG. Item 2: call without a URL now says a URL is required and why; IRC structurally cannot host a keyed call. Tests in mimid-agent/tests/irc_v2.rs; documented in mimid-agent-irc's lib.rs and docs/agent.md. The invite gap is bead mimid-1wgh.130.
